text:
incident-bot: PAGE: SEV=P1 urgent - elevated tail latency and queueing for hosted inference (tenant: tenant-42). impact: failed requests & timeouts. link: https://redwood.in/ops/inc/1769998888 :rotating_light:

sam oncall: taking this, oncall here. first check: which routes impacted?

nina: /v1/generate and /v1/chat heavy for tenant-42. metric: runtime.max_inflight for their slice at 820/200 (configured). queue depth spiked to 1200, avg p99 latency 4.8s -> timeouts.

lee-runtime: thanks. looks like tenant spike from a new A/B test. two immediate live mitigations we can do: 1) carve out tenant-42 quota to soft-limit them, 2) disable streaming+large-context variant for that tenant. both fast.

marta-support: I can draft quick customer note once we know action. need ETA for restore.

jordan-sre: agree with carveout. also consider lowering global max_inflight on overloaded nodes to prevent noisy neighbor. but prefer per-tenant first.

sam oncall: propose plan: (A) create tenant carveout: reduce tenant concurrency to 3 and rate limit to 5 rps, (B) toggle off streaming for tenant-42, (C) increase eviction aggressiveness: lower max_idle_ms and shorten request_timeout for their slice.

lee-runtime: commands ready. running now:
```
# create per-tenant carveout
POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/tenants/tenant-42/mitigate
{
  "concurrency": 3,
  "rate_limit_rps": 5,
  "disable_features": ["streaming","kv-prefetch-large"]
}
# adjust runtime eviction policy for tenant slice
POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/runtime/slices/tenant-42/scale
{
  "eviction_window_ms": 200,
  "request_timeout_ms": 20000
}
```

nina: ack. watching metrics.

sam oncall: I applied the carveout and feature toggle (curl-sent). monitoring now.

nina: immediate improvement: queue depth down from 1200 -> 260 in ~45s. p99 latency from 4.8s -> 2.1s. error rate fallen from 12% -> 3%.

jordan-sre: good. we should also shard their requests away from hot nodes (traffic-shaper). lee can you rotate their traffic to lower-loaded hosts?

lee-runtime: doing a traffic-slice move: `trafficctl move tenant-42 -> slice-b` (slice-b has spare capacity). kicked it, will rebalance in ~30s.

sam oncall: after rebalance: queuing continues to drop, overall latency trending down. still seeing a handful of 504s for long-running requests.

lee-runtime: plan B if we still see tail: enable soft-shedding on tenant-42 for requests above 10s, return 429 with retry-after. config:
```
PATCH /runtime/config
{
  "shedding": {
    "tenant": "tenant-42",
    "policy": "latency_based",
    "threshold_ms": 10000,
    "response": 429
  }
}
```

sam oncall: hold on enabling 429s until we confirm with support on customer comms. marta, can you prepare a short heads-up saying we throttled some requests to protect platform health?

marta-support: drafting now:
"Hi team at Tenant-42 — we observed a traffic surge causing request failures. We applied temporary limits (reduced concurrency, disabled streaming) to stabilize service. You may see slower responses or 429s. We're monitoring and will share updates. ETA for full restoration ~30-60m."

nina: after carveout + move: infra metrics stable. cpu/gpu utilization normalized on hot hosts. p99 now ~1.9s. no new errors in last 2m.

jordan-sre: keep the mitigation for at least 20m to confirm, then we can slowly relax. include rollback plan: revert carveout and re-enable streaming in controlled steps.

lee-runtime: logging mitigation change set to audit. command history saved to /ops/actions/1769998888.log.

sam oncall: setting a follow-up check in 20m. if stable, we'll remove carveout and re-enable streaming with staged rollout.

marta-support: sent the message to tenant-42 support channel. they replied: "Thanks — we're rolling back the A/B test, will confirm when done."

nina: note for post-incident: add tenant detection rule to alert earlier when per-tenant inflight > configured_max by 200%.

sam oncall: agreed. I'll file the follow-up ticket.

jordan-sre: nice work. closing pager for now but keep this thread open for rollback steps. :thumbsup:
